source_binding.mechanism: mutation testing plus distinguishing kill-profile diversity for acceptance-checker calibration

public_sources.claim_used: Diversity-aware mutation adequacy distinguishes mutants by the sets of tests that kill them, explicitly encouraging more diverse tests rather than only a one-dimensional total kill count.
Mutation testing deliberately changes behavior; a mutant is killed when a test fails and survives when tests do not detect the change.
Surviving mutations identify behavioral changes that the current tests do not detect, exposing test blind spots.

source_binding.literal_external_runtime_reason: No Stryker, Mutatest, CI, compiler, hosted runner, external model, or cloud execution is on the accepted path. The four mutants and checker outcomes are finite constructed controller artifacts evaluated directly in Chat.
source_binding.chat_native_reduction: Use a predeclared matrix of known-bad controller-output mutations. Treat a checker as killing a mutant when its fixed rule rejects that mutant. A checker pair is eligible only when the union kills every required mutant and each checker contributes at least one unique kill.

scope_limit: Constructed four-mutant calibration only. Differential kill profiles do not prove checker independence outside this mutant set or guarantee coverage of unknown common-mode faults.
unresolved_child: Mutation calibration itself can overfit a fixed mutant set. A later leaf should test mutation-set rotation/holdout or unseen-fault calibration without consuming quota-bearing infrastructure.
